skill.name: explore-run

content.value_statement: Exploratory training can consume budgets without producing comparable evidence. This skill ranks limited variants and records results for careful human review.
actual_capabilities: Builds candidate variants from parameter axes, subset sizes, and short-run step limits.
Scores variants using cost, predicted success, and expected gain.
Prunes candidates using maximum variant and short-cycle run budgets.
Supports custom selection weights, primary metrics, and optimization direction.
Defines output reports for changes, comparability, top runs, and status.
limitations: Requires explicit researcher authorization before exploratory execution.
Plans and ranks experiments but delegates actual training execution to other skills.
Heuristic scores are not evidence of model quality or successful execution.
Shared reference and writer files may require the original repository structure.

use_cases.title: Screen Training Variants
use_cases.description: Create a small candidate matrix before committing resources to full training.

use_cases.title: Prioritize Idle GPU Work
use_cases.description: Rank bounded experiments by estimated cost, success probability, and expected gain.

use_cases.title: Review Exploratory Evidence
use_cases.description: Document comparability limits and top candidates before approving further validation.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Small Probe
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan a small-subset probe for [research goal]. Use [subset size] and [step limit]. Keep the trusted baseline unchanged.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner planning for one bounded experiment

prompt_templates.title: Create a Variant Matrix
prompt_templates.prompt: Build variants for [parameter axes]. Limit the plan to [maximum variants] and [maximum short-cycle runs]. Rank candidates conservatively.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate comparison across several parameter choices

prompt_templates.title: Tune Selection Priorities
prompt_templates.prompt: Rank candidates using these weights: cost [value], success rate [value], and expected gain [value]. Explain the highest-ranked choices.

prompt_templates.title: Assess Executed Runs
prompt_templates.prompt: Review results for [primary metric] with a [maximize or minimize] goal. Separate measured evidence from heuristic predictions and note unfair comparisons.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced evidence review after exploratory execution

output_examples.input: Plan learning-rate probes on a ten-percent subset with three short runs.
output_examples.output: A ranked list of three bounded variants, estimated costs, selection reasons, and baseline isolation requirements.

output_examples.input: Compare completed runs using validation loss as the minimized metric.
output: Top runs ordered by measured validation loss.
Comparability notes for changed subsets or step limits.
A clear statement that exploratory results need trusted validation.

output_examples.input: Reduce a large variant grid to four affordable candidates.
output_examples.output: Four budget-compliant candidates ranked by the configured cost, success, and gain weights.

best_practices: Get explicit approval before planning or launching exploratory runs.
Start with small subsets and short cycles before using larger budgets.
Keep exploratory state separate and report every comparability limitation.
anti_patterns: Do not treat heuristic rankings as measured research results.
Do not modify or promote the trusted baseline automatically.
Do not claim state-of-the-art performance from bounded exploratory evidence.

faq.question: Does this skill run training commands?
faq.answer: It focuses on planning and summaries. Actual command execution can be handed to dedicated execution skills.

faq.question: Can it explore without approval?
faq.answer: No. The policy requires explicit researcher authorization for exploratory work.

faq.question: How are candidates ranked?
faq.answer: Candidates receive weighted scores for cost efficiency, predicted success, and expected gain.

faq.question: Can I change the ranking weights?
faq.answer: Yes. Provide selection weights for cost, success rate, and expected gain.

faq.question: Does a high score prove improvement?
faq.answer: No. Pre-execution scores are heuristic and must be replaced by measured evidence after runs.

faq.question: What reports should it produce?
faq.answer: Expected outputs cover changes, scientific history, comparability, top runs, and current status.
